title: Work like you’re not a mother, mother like you don’t work. It’s impossible
content:
Picture this. It’s 8pm on a Thursday. My two girls, six and eight, are in the sittingroom. The room is dark, except for a disco ball strobe light shooting out colours across the ceiling and walls, and the Disney Zombies soundtrack is blaring.
The pair bop to the music in their PJs, swirling around the room, jumping on and off the couch singing out the lyrics. The shutters are vibrating, a water bottle teeters on the edge of a table. Popcorn is on the floor.
They are having a ball. And I am at the kitchen table working.
I am just one of the more than 1.3 million women in employment in Ireland.
READ MORE
According to the CSO, female participation in the Irish workforce has jumped 90 per cent since 2000.
And it stands to reason that more women in the workforce than ever before means more working mothers than ever before.
Being a working mother is a horror show at times. The stress can be crippling. You are expected to be everything to everyone.
You are expected to be a solid, reliable employee; an ambitious career go-getter; to command meetings in clothes without spit-up or Weetabix on them on three hours sleep and all while also being Suzy Homemaker come 5pm cooking dinner from scratch and making sure your little darlings are thriving in every way possible.
Work like you’re not a mother, mother like you don’t work. It’s an impossible standard.
This particular Thursday, believe it or not, my stress levels are low, around a three. My husband is in Belfast for the night so I am on my own. Yes, I have things to do but the dancing duo in the sittingroom are old enough to, mostly, fend for themselves, be quiet when I need them to be and, almost, put themselves to bed.
Being a working mum in the early years is an entirely different beast. Whenever I see a new mum who is thriving, I am in awe. Especially if it is her first child.
After having my first baby, I was a smidgen unhinged. Often bawling, overwhelmed and anxious. She didn’t sleep; so neither did I and I overthought everything. It took a long time to feel anywhere normal.
With a new mortgage to pay and just 26 weeks of statutory maternity leave to work with, Lily started creche before she was one and I headed back to work, a woman on the edge.
Whereas before, I only had to deal with a small baby and my unhinged-ness, now I had to pretend I was a fully functioning human woman capable of working five days a week without ripping apart at the seams.
The guilt was devastating. I left her at creche before 9am and sometimes collected her after 6pm. I thought of her constantly.
My creche’s USP was they had cameras in their rooms so you could log in and view your child. I clocked up hours staring at that CCTV. Looking at the grainy back of her head as she listened to Julia Donaldson’s latest tome at story time, or watching as she tottered around the room with her little pals.
And the guilt is only a tiny part of being a working mother in the early years. You tie yourself up in knots trying to get everything done. And become exhausted from doing it all.
A new child in creche gets sick instantly and has a lurgy for a solid two years.
Pre-Covid this was a nightmare, as most people, me included, were expected to be in the office five days a week. That sinking feeling when the creche’s number pops up on the phone – the PTSD is only abating now.
Once working from home became prevalent post-Covid, that particular stress diminished, but rather than take the day off, you now work from home beside your sick child, pale and listless on the couch. Catching puke in buckets while catching up on emails.
I asked a few friends about their more memorable “working mother” moments.
One told me how, while pregnant, she would pretend the doorbell rang when she was on a Teams call just so she could be sick and then she would pop back on like nothing had happened.
Another remembered doing a radio interview while literally running away from a bleating toddler who was supposed to be napping.
Then there are the mundane and ordinary occurrences like taking calls while breastfeeding, attending work conferences online with a sick and sleeping baby on your lap, being interrupted mid-sentence with “Maaaammmmy” and fighting fires outside of work hours while trying to wrangle a toddler.
For the new and growing group of working mothers in Ireland – I think the collective noun must be an “exhaustive of working mothers” – what’s being done to relieve them of some of this stress? Flexible working hours, understanding bosses and companies, legislative protections, higher pay. All this and more, but right now, I don’t have time to ponder, my two dancing divas need to go to bed and I need to finish my shift.

title: Disabled Pets at Home worker wins £18k after being forced to walk upstairs to use toilet
content:
Disabled Pets at Home worker wins £18k after being forced to walk upstairs to use toilet
The worker only saw change when she resorted to emailing bosses saying ‘Does anyone care?’

A disabled Pets at Home worker has won over £18,000 after she was forced to walk up three flights of stairs to the toilet because she was not told about the disabled toilet for five months.
Mihaela Bonciog - who suffered from chronic back pain and bladder issues - had to struggle up three flights of stairs for nearly half a year because bosses didn't tell her she had access to a ground-floor toilet.
Ms Bonciog told of the daily 'fear' she experienced that her colleagues would see her wet herself due to her incontinence episodes and said over time it became 'psychological suffering'.
She also wasn't given the ergonomic chair she asked for to help with her debilitating back pain for four months.
Ms Bonciog, who worked in a Pets at Home warehouse, only saw change when she resorted to emailing bosses saying "Does anyone care?"
At Cambridge Employment Tribunal, Ms Bonciog won her claims of a failure to make reasonable adjustments for her disability, which is a form of disability discrimination.
She won compensation of £18,277.
She started working in the Pets at Home warehouse in August 2016.
In February 2021, Ms Bonciog was diagnosed with lower back pain after lifting a heavy box and took a week off work because she was struggling to walk, but she did not think she needed any adjustments made.
She reported back pain several times for the next two years, but in August 2023 she informed her managers that she had been diagnosed as having a herniated disc in her back.
Ms Bonciog had an occupational health assessment carried out in October 2023, and this said that she needed adjustments to be made so that she had a workstation assessment to change her chair and that she have access to a closer bathroom for her urinary incontinence.
It also said that she should not lift anything heavy and she should not be asked to stand for long periods of time.
Ms Bonciog went on sick leave because of her back pain for a month starting in November 2023.
Despite following up about a workstation assessment, this was only carried out in May 2024 and an ergonomic chair was bought for Ms Bonciog.
She emailed saying: "No one has provided me a proper chair or a fob to the nearest toilet. Does anyone care?"
Pets at Home said that she had been granted permission to use the ground floor toilet, but they had not informed her that she could have access to a key fob to use that toilet.
Employment Judge Andrea Booth ruled that there was a failure to make reasonable adjustments because Pets at Home failed to provide an appropriate chair and did not tell Ms Bonciog she had access to a ground floor toilet.
She said: "[Pets at Home] recognised the urgency and need for a reasonable adjustment to give [Ms Bonciog] easier access to a toilet because this was actioned very quickly, by 7 November 2023.
"However, the [company] failed to communicate this to [her] until 17 May 2024, leaving her without the reasonable adjustment.
"The Tribunal has found that the period of the failure to make this reasonable adjustment for the purposes of this complaint is from 7 November 2023 to 29 March 2024; a period of almost 5 months.
"[She] was left in an uncertain situation with poor communication from the [company] and an apparent lack of action.
"[She] asked about the ergonomic chair in the welcome back to work meeting on 29 December 2023 and in an email of 22 March 2024.
"[She] also asked about access to a toilet in her email of 22 March 2024, which concluded with the question “does anyone care?”, which the Tribunal finds indicates that [she] was distressed and felt that the [company] did not care about her."
Judge Booth said that this situation caused Ms Bonciog a lot of stress as she worried she would be 'humiliated' if she wet herself in front of her colleagues.
She said: "In [Ms Bonciog's] schedule of loss, she described that she has been experiencing stress and has been taking Sertraline 50mg per day on a prescription since 2023 to help her manage the impact of stress and anxiety.
"She also described that she has experienced physical and psychological suffering including walking up and down the stairs to reach the toilet, struggling with back pain and bladder leaking, and being afraid that colleagues will see her wet herself.
"In [her] submissions on remedy, she described that for almost five months she was required to use a toilet that was three flights of stairs away and the practical effect was daily risk and reality of incontinence episodes, together with associated embarrassment and anxiety.
"She also described that the failure to provide her with an ergonomic chair exacerbated her back pain.
"She went on to say: 'No amount of compensation can undo the chronic pain I lived with, or the fear I carried every day – of walking two flights down and one flight back up just to reach a toilet all the while afraid of an accident happening in front of my colleagues.
"That fear, and the humiliation it threatened, stayed with me throughout this period.'
"The Tribunal finds that the risk of humiliation arising from urinary incontinence and difficulty in accessing a toilet bore great significance for [her]."
Ms Bonciog made other claims of disability discrimination and unpaid holiday pay, but these were unsuccessful.

title: Man who weighed 48st manages to lose 32st without GLP-1s. Here’s how
content:
Man who weighed 48st manages to lose 32st without GLP-1s. Here’s how
Tiny said he got his ‘ironic’ nickname of Tiny aged 10 because he has ‘always stood out in a crowd’ for his height and weight
- Bookmark
- CommentsGo to comments
A father who lost 32st after being cautioned that his size endangered his life during open-heart surgery now believes he has the "best chance" of staying with his family.
Standing 6ft 8in tall, 46-year-old maintenance business owner Mark Bailey, from Stockton, Warwickshire, was nicknamed Tiny and was a "big lad" from a young age. Having been "on the heavier side" since childhood, he hit a peak weight of 48st 9lbs (309kg) aged 39, requiring 7XL tops and 72-inch waist trousers.
His weight soared after years of consuming 7,500 calories daily, including pasties and Mars bars for breakfast, McDonald’s lunches, kebabs for dinner, and unmonitored beer consumption.
A heart murmur diagnosis in October 2021 prompted the need for open-heart surgery, serving as a "wake-up call" to "be around" for his wife, Nicola Bailey, and their children, Kyla, 26, Byron, 23, and Kyson, 17.
Declining GLP-1 medication and weight loss surgery, he lost 28st (177kg) across four years through lifestyle changes ahead of his October 2025 operation. Following a successful procedure, he shed an additional 4st (25kg) and recently finished a 5km challenge for the Rugby Cardiac Rehabilitation team.
Tiny told PA Real Life: “When I had a chat with the cardiologist … she said if I had open-heart surgery at the weight I was, the chances of me coming off that operating table were very, very slim.
“I knew I got myself in this position, so I could get myself out of it.
“It’s frightening, but you can have such a good life afterwards and I’m already proving that now.”
Tiny said he got his “ironic” nickname of Tiny aged 10 because he has “always stood out in a crowd” for his height and weight.
“I’ve always been a food lover and it just escalated,” he said.
“I just never limited myself to anything, so I had what I wanted when I wanted it.”
On an average day, Tiny said he consumed around 7,500 calories, starting with a full English breakfast of five sausages, five rashers of bacon, five hash browns and five eggs, before having a packet of crisps, a soft drink and chocolate bars as a mid-morning snack.
For lunch, he tended to have McDonald’s, with his order consisting of a double quarter pounder, two double cheeseburgers, fries, mozzarella sticks and a large milkshake.
His dinner was often an extra large doner kebab with cheesy chips and garlic bread, and he always finished the night with a packet of biscuits.
Tiny has had health complications over the years, including being diagnosed with the thyroid immune condition Graves’ disease at age 34, as well as sore knees, gallbladder issues and shoulder pain.
As a result, he tried “a few” ways to lose weight, including the carnivore diet, which is based mainly on eating meat and other animal products, and Slimming World, with some success.
But after being diagnosed with a heart murmur in October 2021, he was told he needed open-heart surgery and that his weight would pose additional risks.
Tiny said he was offered bariatric surgery to shrink his stomach and weight-loss jabs but declined both, as he did not want any further medical interventions.
Instead, Tiny “did a lot of research” and implemented a calorie deficit, cutting out biscuits and chocolate bars, and started going to the gym twice a week.
Within two years, he lost 18st (114kg) but said he still felt mentally and emotionally “rubbish” because he was experiencing breathlessness and “horrible palpitations” because of his failing heart health.
A routine scan in September 2025 confirmed his valve got worse so they could not put off the open-heart surgery any longer.
“The surgeon actually said my valve didn’t have six weeks left in it, so he agreed to cut short his holiday for me to get me fixed up,” Tiny said.
On October 15, Tiny had the seven-hour surgery at University Hospital Coventry. He said his recovery was “really quite fast” and he was discharged after eight days.
Tiny started at the Cardiac Rehabilitation Service in Rugby for eight weeks from December, across 16 “very steady” and supervised sessions.
“The surgeon did a fantastic job and the nurses at Coventry Hospital were absolutely brilliant,” Tiny said.
“But Rugby Cardiac Rehabilitation went above and beyond.
“They gave me the confidence to know what my heart can and can’t take and how far I can push myself.”
As a way to say thank you to his rehabilitation team, Tiny completed the 5km Autumn Wolf wild muddy obstacle run – an off-road course through obstacles, mud and water – on September 11 this year.
Tiny said: “I absolutely loved it … and it was my own personal challenge to see how well this heart works.
“I was jumping off bridges, climbing up riverbanks, running through fields, rope climbing, climbing walls – all stuff that I never thought I’d be able to do again.
“But I’ve proven that I can do it and I really enjoyed it.”
Tiny now weighs 16st 11lbs (106kg), wearing a size large and 38in waist trousers, and has even lost two shoe sizes, going from a 15 to a 13.
Some people have jokingly started calling him Biggie, instead of his “less ironic” nickname Tiny, but he said it still works for his height.
Tiny’s average daily meals now consist of a shot of turmeric, ginger, cayenne pepper and apple cider vinegar first thing in the morning before a gym workout, high protein foods, as well as fresh fruit, vegetables and water throughout the day.
He wanted to thank his wife Nicola in particular, who he said has been his “rock” throughout, and he is thankful he can enjoy a future getting to know his 18-month-old granddaughter, Ellena.
“I love going to the gym or for a run with my wife and I enjoy the foods I eat,” Tiny said.
“I’ve given myself the best chance in life now and I’ve gone out my way to improve everything and make sure that I’m around for my kids and my wife.”
Looking back on his progress, he said: “I made a mistake by letting myself go by eating rubbish.
“It’s the same as having a car – if you put decent fuel in, it’ll last you a lifetime.”

title: „Krone“-Vereinsserie - Bis auf Olympia hat dieser Klub alles erlebt
content:
Die Möve Salzburg gibt es schon seit 1923. In dieser langen Zeit hat der Ruderverein sehr viel erlebt. Nach dem 2. Weltkrieg wurde dieser vor dem Land Salzburg befreit. Im Küstenrudern hat man aktuell Hoffnungsträger.
Kaum ein Sportverein in Salzburg hat eine solche Geschichte wie der Ruderklub Möve Salzburg. Gegründet hat sich der Verein am 10. Februar 1923, das erste Bootshaus wurde an der Salzach im Bereich des heutigen Aya-Bades errichtet. „Angeblich“, erzählt Ehrenpräsident Gottfried Eisinger, „hat man den Verein so benannt, weil es damals so viele Möwen an der Salzach gegeben hat.“ Bald stellten die Gründer um Fritz Wonka fest, dass der Fluss für einen Ruderbetrieb ungeeignet war, so übersiedelte man an den Wallersee und blieb bis heute dort.
Danach wurde es turbulent: Im Anschlussjahr 1938 wurde die Möve in den nationalsozialistischen Reichsbund für Leibesübungen eingegliedert. Das Ende des Zweiten Weltkrieges war auch ein Ende des Rudervereins, weil er als Vereinsvermögen von den Alliierten beschlagnahmt wurde. „Die Möve war die erste Institution, die von den Amerikanern befreit worden ist, noch bevor Salzburg befreit wurde“, erklärt Eisinger.
Jahr für Jahr feierte die Möve Salzburg Erfolge
Danach begann für den Klub der Wiederaufbau. Die erste Herbstregatta 1951 am Wallersee war mit mehr als 100 Teilnehmern einer der größten Sportevents in der Nachkriegszeit in Salzburg. In den 70er Jahren begann die Arbeit von Professor Dietmar Mühlfellner Früchte zu tragen. Jahr für Jahr feierte die Möve Erfolge (1975 waren es 96 Vereinssiege).
1995 übernahm Eisinger die Leitung des Leistungszentrums. Mit Ralph Kreibich ging daraus das bislang größte Möve-Talent hervor, das sich 2007 im Einer zum Europameister krönte. Mit der Gründung des Küstenruderns und dem EM-Titel von Tabea Minichmayr 2024 sowie dem Junioren-WM-Titel 2025 von Nikolas Roidmayer mit Caroline Schwendinger setzt der Verein, dessen rund 155 Mitglieder pro Jahr gesamt bis zu 40.000 Kilometer rudern, hier seine Erfolge fort. Doch Eisinger weiß, was in dieser bemerkenswerten Geschichte fehlt: „Von der Möve war noch nie jemand bei Olympia.“

title: Karnataka homestay owner’s arrest over US woman’s rape illegal: Supreme Court
content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday upheld the Karnataka High Court order declaring illegal the arrest of the owner of a homestay in Kodagu where a US national was allegedly sexually assaulted in April.
The high court, which also directed the state government to pay the homestay owner Rs 5 lakh in compensation, said in its July 15 order that “a citizen’s fundamental rights cannot be bartered away simply because of pressure from foreign embassies”.
A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta dismissed an appeal filed by the state government, which argued that the homestay owner was informed of the grounds of his arrest, the fact of his arrest was intimated to his relative, and he was produced before the jurisdictional magistrate within the stipulated period. It further argued that the police had a duty to take him into custody to conduct a preliminary investigation because the FIR contained cognisable offences.
The homestay owner and an employee were arrested after the American embassy forwarded a complaint stating that the employee spiked the tourist’s drink and sexually assaulted her on April 12 while she stayed there.
The police picked up the homestay owner on the evening of April 18, detained him overnight, and recorded his arrest at 5 am the following morning. The FIR was registered under charges of rape, criminal intimidation, and concealing design to commit an offence.
Rape charge against homestay owner ‘wholly incongruous’
After reviewing the case diary, the high court noted that the homestay owner was admittedly not present when the crime occurred and had no direct role in it.
The high court had ruled that charging the homestay owner with rape was “wholly incongruous”. The remaining charges, dealing with the omission of information or the disappearance of evidence, were non-cognisable.
Invoking landmark Supreme Court rulings, the high court said that arrest is not a “ritualistic exercise” or a starting tool for investigation.
The homestay owner has also moved a contempt petition in the high court as he has not received the compensation, which the government was to pay within four weeks of the court order.

title: Over 720,000 travellers passed through the new Singapore Cruise Centre since July 15
content:
Over 720,000 travellers passed through the new Singapore Cruise Centre since July 15
SINGAPORE – The new Singapore Cruise Centre (HarbourFront) has processed more than 720,000 travellers since full operations began on July 15, leveraging automated systems to handle up to 18,000 departing travellers a day during peak periods.
A new system consolidates real-time data from ferry and cruise operators every step of the way – from check-in to boarding. This enables the operators and the Singapore Cruise Centre (SCC) to enhance coordination and better manage the flow of travellers.
The standalone terminal, which replaces the former terminal at HarbourFront Centre, was designed to make the passenger experience more intuitive, said SCC chairman Loh Lik Peng.
Speaking at the terminal’s official opening on Sept 22, he highlighted its various amenities, including passport-less immigration lanes, self-service check-in kiosks and baggage drop-off points.
All five ferry operators – Batam Fast Ferry, Horizon Fast Ferry, Majestic Fast Ferry, Sindo Ferry and Indo Falcon Shipping and Travel – have counters on the ground floor of the building.
These were previously spread across two floors at the old terminal.
Senior Minister of State for Transport Murali Pillai, who was guest of honour at the opening, said: “As travel patterns evolve, technology and innovation will be increasingly important in making these experiences smoother and more effortless.
“The upgraded HarbourFront terminal reflects this commitment – combining automation and thoughtful uses of space to improve the passenger experience.”
Describing the terminal as “extremely comfortable”, Batam resident Hasim, who goes by one name, said it was a huge upgrade over the old facility.
The 45-year-old maritime industry worker said the new facility looked clean and bright, and that the process of checking in and boarding was quicker and more efficient.
However, he had one complaint: The new building is farther from the MRT, even though it is connected to HarbourFront station.
“It used to be a much shorter walk, and you didn’t have to go outdoors,” he said in Bahasa Indonesia.
Retiree Roland Lim likes that there are snacks for sale before departure, as well as the convenience of having all the ferry operator counters on the ground floor.
The 67-year-old, who was headed to Batam to play golf, said: “It’s way easier than back then. And if you’re comfortable doing self-service, there’s that option too, so I appreciate how accessible things are.”

title: Nữ võ sĩ 3 lần vô địch muay thế giới được trao học bổng 50% học phí
content:
Cách đây vài ngày, nữ võ sĩ Huỳnh Hà Hữu Hiếu cùng đội tuyển muay Việt Nam kết thúc Giải vô địch Muay thế giới 2026 tại Kosovo. Ở chung kết hạng cân 45kg nữ hệ vô địch, cô thắng Anastassiya Konyushko của Kazakhstan với tỉ số 30-25, giành huy chương vàng.
Đây là lần thứ ba liên tiếp Hữu Hiếu giành huy chương vàng hạng cân 45kg nữ tại Giải vô địch Muay thế giới, sau các năm 2024 và 2025. Cô hiện thi đấu cho thể thao TP.HCM và đội tuyển muay Việt Nam, đồng thời là võ sĩ Việt Nam duy nhất giành huy chương vàng đối kháng ở hệ vô địch tại giải năm nay.
Hôm nay 18-9, Trường đại học Hùng Vương TP.HCM tổ chức gặp mặt, tuyên dương Hữu Hiếu, trao giấy khen và học bổng tương đương 50% học phí toàn khóa. Nữ võ sĩ hiện là học viên năm 2 chương trình văn bằng 2 ngành ngôn ngữ Anh của trường.
Tại buổi giao lưu, Hữu Hiếu trải lòng từng trải qua giai đoạn chấn thương chân. Sau điều trị, chân vẫn còn đau trong quá trình tập luyện và có những bài cô phải nén đau để hoàn thành.
Lịch tập luyện, thi đấu cũng khiến Hữu Hiếu có thời điểm không thể đến lớp trực tiếp. Cô duy trì việc học online để không bỏ dở chương trình.
Hữu Hiếu cho biết từng khá ấp úng trong một lần trả lời báo chí quốc tế tại Malaysia. Sau khoảng nửa năm học ngành ngôn ngữ Anh, cô nhận thấy khả năng nghe hiểu tốt hơn và tự tin hơn khi trả lời phỏng vấn bằng tiếng Anh.
"Với em, kẻ thù lớn nhất không phải là đối thủ trên sàn đấu, mà chính là bản thân mình. Nếu mình không cố gắng hết sức, mình sẽ tạo ra sức ì và rất khó bước ra khỏi giới hạn của chính mình", Hữu Hiếu chia sẻ.
Cô nói mình cố gắng vượt qua giới hạn ấy trong từng buổi tập, từng trận đấu và cả việc học.
HLV Cổ Tấn Anh Linh - người trực tiếp dẫn dắt Hữu Hiếu - cho biết học trò có biệt danh "Ốc tiêu". Không có lợi thế về thể hình, Hữu Hiếu bù lại bằng tốc độ, kỹ thuật và bản lĩnh, nhất là trong những trận đấu lớn.
Ông đánh giá cao sự kiên trì của cô trong những thời điểm gặp chấn thương và quá trình trở lại tập luyện.
TS Nguyễn Thị Mỹ Dung - Phó hiệu trưởng Trường đại học Hùng Vương TP.HCM - cho rằng với một vận động viên thường xuyên tập luyện, thi đấu và di chuyển, việc duy trì học tập cần sự phối hợp giữa nhà trường, đơn vị huấn luyện và chính người học để có kế hoạch phù hợp.
Theo bà Dung, kiến thức và năng lực nghề nghiệp sẽ giúp Hữu Hiếu có thêm lựa chọn sau giai đoạn thi đấu đỉnh cao. Nhà trường muốn nữ võ sĩ tiếp tục duy trì việc học, tích lũy kiến thức và kỹ năng trong thời gian còn theo đuổi thể thao thành tích cao.

title: 33,600 more get jobs, but SA’s unemployment crisis deepens
content:
Story audio is generated using AI
The department of employment and labour says it placed 33,600 job seekers in employment and other opportunities during the first quarter of the 2026/27 financial year, as South Africa grapples with an unemployment rate of 33.6%.
The figures were disclosed in a parliamentary response after MK Party MP Siyabonga Percival Mkhize questioned employment and labour minister Nomakhosazana Meth on what interventions her department had implemented to create permanent and sustainable employment rather than temporary work opportunities.
Mkhize also asked how many permanent jobs had resulted from each intervention, how much had been spent and what measurable targets the department had set to reduce unemployment by the end of the financial year.
Meth said more than 456,000 unemployed job seekers were registered on the department’s Employment Services of South Africa (Essa) system during the first quarter.
“In the 2026/27 financial year, quarter one, the department provided various services to the unemployed work seekers. Work seekers that were enrolled on the department’s Essa system totalled 456,094, counselling services that were provided totalled 144,104, and the number of work seekers placed, for quarter one of 2026, equalled to 33,600,” she said.
Meth said the 33,600 placements included formal jobs, apprenticeships, project opportunities and training opportunities.
Limpopo had the highest number of placements at 8,688, followed by Gauteng with 7,238.
The Eastern Cape recorded 3,797 placements, KwaZulu-Natal 3,290, Free State 2,639, Western Cape 2,554 and Mpumalanga 2,174.
The Northern Cape recorded 1,613 placements while North West had the lowest number at 1,607.
The figures come as the country’s unemployment rate climbed to its highest level in four years. Stats SA’s Quarterly Labour Force Survey for the second quarter of 2026 showed the official unemployment rate increased from 32.7% in the first quarter to 33.6%.
The number of unemployed people increased by 345,000 to 8.5-million, while the number of employed people decreased by 16,000 to 16.7-million.
Young people continue to bear a disproportionate share of the unemployment crisis. The number of unemployed people aged between 15 and 34 years old increased by 264,000 to 5-million between the first and second quarters.
The youth unemployment rate increased by 1.5 percentage points to 47.4%, while the number of employed young people declined by 40,000 to 5.6-million.
On the cost of its employment interventions, Meth said public employment services were offered free of charge and funded through the department’s overall budget, meaning there was no specific amount allocated to each service.
“For the 2026/27 financial year, given the budget allocated, the department will target placing 75,000 work seekers into employment opportunities, and a further 130,000 job opportunities will be targeted through its partnership with the National Pathway Management Network. The department aims to create 1-million work opportunities as part of its MTDP target, plus a further 1-million by its entities,” said Meth.
The department’s first-quarter figure of 33,600 represents about 45% of its annual target of placing 75,000 work seekers into employment opportunities.
The department’s response did not provide a breakdown of how many of the 33,600 placements were permanent jobs, as opposed to apprenticeships, project or training opportunities.

title: Tchad : COPIDEV renforce l'autonomie économique des femmes du canton de Bédaya
content:
Tchad : COPIDEV renforce l'autonomie économique des femmes du canton de Bédaya
Le COPIDEV a remis des équipements de couture au groupement féminin « Kãa Keté Ya Diangue » à Bédaya, afin de renforcer son autonomie financière dans le cadre du projet Gang « Do Ya Diangue ».
Par Elwood Dk
À Bédaya, dans la province du Mandoul, le groupement « Kãa Keté Ya Diangue » bénéficie d’un nouvel accompagnement pour développer ses activités. Le vendredi 18 septembre 2026, le Consortium pour la Promotion des Initiatives de Développement (COPIDEV) lui a remis plusieurs équipements destinés à soutenir principalement les travaux de couture. Machines à coudre, tissus, fer à repasser, tables et autres accessoires font partie du matériel cédé au groupement.
Cette dotation intervient dans le cadre du projet Gang « Do Ya Diangue », qui cherche à renforcer les activités génératrices de revenus et à améliorer l’autonomie financière des bénéficiaires.
La cheffe de projet, Mme Hassanié Getty Charlotte, estime que ces équipements constituent un moyen supplémentaire pour les membres du groupement de consolider leurs activités et de progresser vers une plus grande indépendance économique. « Cet appui doit permettre aux bénéficiaires de travailler dans de meilleures conditions, d’augmenter leur production et de mieux organiser leurs activités », a-t-elle précisé.
De son côté, l’animateur du projet, Allahramadji Madji Ngario, a souligné que cette remise de matériel marque une nouvelle étape dans l’accompagnement du groupement. Il s’agit notamment de consolider les résultats déjà obtenus et d’encourager les bénéficiaires à poursuivre leurs initiatives.
Pour les femmes du groupement « Kãa Keté Ya Diangue » du canton de Bédaya, ce matériel arrive comme un appui pratique pour améliorer leur travail quotidien. Il devrait également leur permettre de développer davantage leurs activités de couture et de renforcer leur collaboration au sein de la structure.
Financé par le Fonds des femmes pour la paix et l’humanitaire, à travers l’UNFPA, cet accompagnement vise à favoriser l’autonomisation économique des femmes et à soutenir les initiatives locales dans le canton de Bédaya.

title: SC orders Indian Oil to pay ₹12L for denying woman job in 1988 ‘just because she is a lady’
content:
SC orders Indian Oil to pay ₹12L for denying woman job in 1988 ‘just because she is a lady’
The court passed the order after noting that Sumitra, a Scheduled Caste woman from Karnal, had turned 63, well beyond the age of superannuation.
The Supreme Court on Thursday directed Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) to pay ₹12 lakh compensation to a Haryana woman who was denied a job as a helper because the oil company considered the work of carrying LPG cylinders unsuitable for women.
A bench of justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi criticised the government undertaking for “disrespecting” women and said, “It is an affront to womanhood and that too by a Government of India undertaking.”
Shortlisted for job in 1988, but not selected
The court passed the order after noting that Sumitra, a Scheduled Caste woman from Karnal, had turned 63, well beyond the age of superannuation, and had spent more than three decades litigating her claim.
The woman had applied for a helper’s job when an LPG bottling plant opened in Karnal in 1988. She was among 49 candidates shortlisted for the post. Although she was educationally qualified and met all the requirements, she was not among the 43 candidates selected. She was later told that she had been denied employment because she was a woman.
IOC, in its response, told the top court, “As the nature of the job and atmosphere and odd working hours in the company of the males was such that petitioner being lady was not considered fit for the job.”
SC rejects Indian Oil's rationale
The bench rejected the rationale, observing: “Day in and day out, when men are not at home, it is the women who lift gas cylinders in the house and change it. And you denied her appointment just because she is a lady. This is disrespect to womanhood.”
Sumitra had first approached the trial court, which in 1990 directed IOC to absorb her in a post other than labourer. IOC challenged the decision before the Punjab and Haryana high court, which overturned it in October 2025. She then approached the Supreme Court.
Also Read: Won’t allow woman officer to be humiliated: Supreme Court to Centre
The bench noted the “long litigation” suffered by Sumitra and said gender was the only ground cited to deny her employment.
“In India, every day we say a woman is a goddess, respect her. This is a fit case for compensation,” the court said.
IOC’s lawyer offered to explore mediation during the hearing, but the bench decided against keeping the matter pending, citing the facts and the delay of more than three decades.
As Sumitra is now beyond the retirement age, the court directed IOC to pay her ₹12 lakh as lump-sum compensation.

title: 30 years after ‘Rs 300 bribe’ charge, MP High Court backs acquittal of land revenue officer
content:
4 min readNew DelhiSep 21, 2026 05:30 PM IST

A 30-year-old bribery case involving an amount of Rs 300 has ended with the Madhya Pradesh High Court upholding the acquittal of a land revenue officer who was accused of demanding the money to issue a duplicate land record.
The court said the recovery of tainted cash alone was not enough to prove bribery, noting that Rs 325 in government dues was already pending against the complainant and that the witnesses differed on key details of the alleged demand.
Justice Sanjeev S Kalgaonkar on September 19 dismissed the state’s appeal and upheld the trial court’s December 1997 acquittal, noting that the circumstances of the case raised the possibility of “resentment and a grudge” between the complainant and the official.




“Rather, their evidence, examined in light of overall circumstances, suggests a reasonable possibility that the amount referred to by the accused (land revenue officer) was meant for payment of outstanding government dues. Thus, the prosecution had failed to establish beyond reasonable doubt that the accused demanded or accepted Rs 300 as ‘illegal gratification’ for issuance of the duplicate Bhu-Adhikar Evam Rin Pustika (land record),” the court observed.
Demanded Rs 300 bribe in 1996
The state said the man was working as a Patwari (land revenue officer) in Sagar district when a complainant approached him for a duplicate Bhu-Adhikar Evam Rin Pustika (land record), after his original document had been misplaced. The prosecution alleged that the officer demanded Rs 450 for issuing the duplicate document. The complainant allegedly paid Rs 150 initially and agreed to pay the remaining Rs 300 later.
Justice Sanjeev S Kalgaonkar said the land revenue official had earlier submitted a report alleging encroachment on government land by the complainant.
The complainant then approached the Lokayukta concerned, which arranged a trap on October 17, 1996. He handed over three marked Rs 100 notes to the officer, and the money was recovered from the Patwari’s shirt pocket. Chemical traces were also found on his hands and shirt pocket.
However, the trial court acquitted him on December 19, 1997, after which the state challenged the decision before the Madhya Pradesh High Court.
Story continues below this ad
‘Paid towards dues’
The state, through advocates Abhinav Shrivastava and Aishwarya Kesarwani, argued that if the evidence of the prosecution is considered in total, then the demand and recovery of bribe money were fully established by the prosecution.
The land revenue official’s lawyer, advocate Aditya S Rajput, argued that Rs 325 was already due from the complainant as government revenue, and his client was instructed to recover the amount before the duplicate document could be issued. The defence, hence, claimed that the money was paid towards the government dues, not a bribe.
Court notes possibility of grudge
The court also noted that the land revenue official had submitted a report on October 3, 1996 alleging encroachment on government land by the complainant. The report was received by the tehsildar’s office on October 5, just days before the bribery complaint was lodged, it noted.
“This circumstance furnishes a plausible cause for the complainant’s resentment and grudge against the accused and assumes significance while assessing his credibility,” the court observed.
Story continues below this ad
The court further found material inconsistencies in the complainant’s account about the amount allegedly demanded, when the demands were made and who was present when they were made. It ultimately held that the prosecution had not proved the bribery allegation beyond reasonable doubt and dismissed the state’s appeal.

title: Enhancing therapeutic outcomes in degenerative lumbar disc disease: a retrospective study on combined autologous PRP injection and celecoxib therapy
content: ObjectiveTo investigate the therapeutic value of autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection in patients with degenerative lumbar disc disease (DLDD), and to evaluate its clinical efficacy in alleviating pain, improving lumbar function, modulating inflammatory responses, and enhancing quality of life.MethodsThis retrospective study included 112 DLDD patients treated at our hospital from April 2023 to February 2025. According to the treatment received, patients were divided into two groups. The control group (n = 56) received oral celecoxib, while the observation group (n = 56) received autologous PRP injection in addition to oral celecoxib. The two groups were compared regarding treatment efficacy, pain response [Visual Analog Scale (VAS)], lumbar function [Japanese Orthopedic Association score (JOA)], disability in daily activities [Oswestry Disability Index (ODI)], inflammatory markers [Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), stromal cell-derived factor-1 (SDF-1)], and incidence of adverse reactions.ResultsThe observation group demonstrated significantly superior overall efficacy compared with the control group (total effective rate: 94.96% vs. 82.14%, P < 0.05). There were significant differences between groups, over time, and in group-time interaction for VAS, JOA, and ODI scores (P < 0.05). At 4 weeks after treatment, TLR4, TNF-α, hs-CRP, and SDF-1 levels in both groups decreased compared with baseline, with greater reductions in the observation group (P < 0.05). The incidence of adverse reactions was similar between groups (8.93% vs. 14.29%, P > 0.05).ConclusionCombining autologous PRP injection with oral celecoxib provides short-term pain relief, functional improvement, and reduction of inflammatory responses in DLDD patients without significantly increasing adverse reactions. However, longer follow-up is required to determine the durability of these effects and the long-term clinical value of PRP-based treatment.

title: Viceministro de Transporte Aéreo reportó una recuperación del 50 % de la operatividad en el Aeropuerto de Maiquetía
content:
El viceministro de Transporte Aéreo y presidente de Bolivariana de Aeropuertos (BAER), Sergio Silvio Prato, reportó que el Aeropuerto Internacional Simón Bolívar de Maiquetía, ubicado en el estado La Guaira, alcanzó un 50 % de su operatividad aérea como resultado de la instalación de terminales temporales.
Dichas instalaciones forman parte de la maniobra de recuperación de las operaciones comerciales que comenzaron el 1° de septiembre, luego de la suspensión de vuelos provocada por los daños estructurales del doble terremoto del 24 de junio.
La información, precisada en una nota de prensa de BAER, resaltó el impacto que han tenido los planes de contingencia para sostener el flujo de usuarios en el recinto aéreo cercano a Caracas.
“El Aeropuerto Internacional Simón Bolívar de Maiquetía consolida su senda de recuperación al alcanzar un 50 % de su operatividad aérea, tras las labores de atención técnica implementadas, luego del evento sísmico del pasado 24 de junio”, se lee en el texto.
Balance de operaciones aéreas
De acuerdo con el balance operativo presentado por las autoridades aeronáuticas, la terminal aérea ha registrado hasta la fecha un total de 1.145 vuelos nacionales, los cuales han permitido el traslado de más de 75 mil usuarios dentro del territorio venezolano.
Con respecto a las rutas internacionales, Silvio Prato detalló que se han contabilizado 576 operaciones comerciales que han movilizado a más de 83 mil viajeros, lo que calificó como un éxito de la función estratégica de Maiquetía para el enlace con el exterior.
Como parte del plan de fortalecimiento de la red aeroportuaria estatal, BAER acotó sobre el desarrollo de obras de adecuación en el Aeropuerto Internacional Arturo Michelena, ubicado en el estado Carabobo.
La institución destacó que, luego del proceso de reversión de sus instalaciones al Estado, ejecutaron trabajos de optimización en la infraestructura de Valencia con el objetivo de responder a la demanda de pasajeros y dinamizar el servicio en la región central del país.
Reincorporación de aerolíneas internacionales
El reporte oficial de BAER anticipó un incremento progresivo en la conectividad aérea internacional del país durante el último trimestre del año, impulsado por el retorno de empresas aeronáuticas extranjeras.
Estas son las aerolíneas que se reincorporarán a la operatividad en Maiquetía:
– Turkish Airlines: reanudará sus operaciones el próximo 1° de octubre con una frecuencia de cuatro vuelos semanales.
– Qatar Airways: tiene previsto retomar sus itinerarios de vuelo hacia el país a partir del 4 de noviembre de este año.
– ITA Airways: adelanta gestiones administrativas para incorporarse a la red de rutas comerciales a partir del año 2027.
BAER agregó que las medidas aéreas para mejorar la conectividad de Venezuela, coordinadas mediante el Ministerio para el Transporte, buscan consolidar la oferta de vuelos comerciales y afianzar la proyección internacional del sistema aeronáutico nacional.

title: A delivery company founded by Arabs takes on its competition in Israel
content:
Deep inside the labyrinthine alleys of Acre’s Old City – home to a 700-year-old Crusader fortress – Muhammad Hani could not order a takeaway pizza. Delivery drivers struggled to navigate the maze of tightly packed ancient buildings, narrow alleyways and winding streets – leaving many of the Arab citizens of Israel there cut off from such services.
“Only the residents like us know how to get around these neighborhoods,” the 27-year-old said.
And even if a driver could find the house address, another barrier remained. Many Arab citizens could only pay with cash, while delivery companies such as Wolt, the leading operator in Israel, only accept card payments. “Most people here don’t have a bank card,” Hani explained.
Launched in 2019, Haat set out to tackle some of the barriers that left communities like Hani’s on the margins of Israel’s high-tech society. Not everyone in the country known as the “Startup Nation” could reap the rewards of cutting-edge services from the latest applications.
At first, the idea for Haat was simple: combine technology with the old-fashioned convenience of cash. But the technology ultimately found uses far beyond its initial goal, helping the Israeli postal service map villages and allowing small, local restaurants to grow a customer base far beyond their neighborhoods.
Founded by Hasan Abasi in the Arab-majority town of Umm al-Fahm in Israel, Haat now offers its services across 50 cities, working with more than 10,000 restaurants and markets, and employing more than 500 couriers. Its success has earned the app a valuation of more than $100 million, according to the company’s PR and Communications lead, Aida Kaddan.
Abasi’s creative strategy with Haat also helped him nab a place on Globes’ 40 Under 40, an annual list by one of Israel’s leading business newspapers recognizing promising young Israelis.
Abasi came up with Haat – Arabic for “bring” – while working for Google in Switzerland. The 36-year-old returned to Umm al-Fahm from Zurich as his wife was expecting a second child. One evening, he tried to order a pizza, but the courier kept getting lost.
The experience helped Abasi recognize a wider problem – and an opportunity. He launched Haat with five others, starting in Umm al-Fahm before expanding to neighboring Arab towns. Demand exploded during the Covid-19 pandemic, when lockdowns kept people at home and online orders boomed.
Abasi was also aware of the systemic issues around banking in Israel, particularly in the Arab sector, where, according to a 2024 study from The National Insurance Institute of Israel, more than 37% live in poverty. Many lower-income families simply don’t have electronic payment options, especially in Umm al-Fahm, according to Mayor Samir Mahamed, making cash the most convenient form of payment.
Like a ‘90s Domino’s delivery
Haat combined the convenience of shopping and dining through a smart phone application with an old-school pay-by-cash option.
This option proved useful beyond Arab communities and has caught on in mixed neighborhoods like Jaffa, where many people do not have bank cards, Kaddan said.
Haat has since expanded its services to allow users also to pay utility and phone bills with cash.
“The cash option came from answering the needs of the society. It has now become one of Haat’s most significant advantages in every area where it operates,” she said.
As Haat focused on reaching those underserved by other delivery applications, its work to turn previously unnavigable streets into mapped-out towns advanced.
Uncharted territory
In some Arab neighbourhoods in Israel, not only were the maze of densely built homes a challenge for delivery services, but streets also often lacked formal names or had unnumbered houses.
“Navigation relied heavily on neighborhood names, family compounds and local landmarks, which posed considerable challenges for postal distribution, commercial deliveries and emergency services,” said Mahamed, the Umm al-Fahm mayor.
Over the past six years, Haat has helped redraw the map of underserved cities. By tracking courier routes and using machine learning to identify roads, neighborhoods, buildings and entrance points overlooked by conventional navigation services, the company says its maps now include 30% more streets in the areas it serves than other mapping platforms.
This was particularly useful for residents in Umm al-Faham, a city of more than 57,000. The mayor said Haat helped support a city-wide project carried out by the local authority to name streets and number houses.
CNN has reached out to Israel’s postal service for comment.
Beyond word-of-mouth
The improved access to Arab neighborhoods also opened up new markets for restaurants and shops overlooked by the wider community, something Haat said “democratizes visibility.”
Krunchy Chicken began as a single fried chicken restaurant in Baqa al-Gharbiyye, an Arab town in northern Israel near the border with the occupied West Bank.
The restaurant has since opened two more branches in the Israeli Triangle – a concentration of Arab towns and villages on the Green Line, which demarcates the boundary between the West Bank and Israel.
At first, Krunchy Chicken relied largely on word-of-mouth advertising, according to manager Sharif Masarweh. But the online exposure of Haat helped greatly, Masarweh told CNN, as did the convenience of different payment options.
“The fact that there is an option for cash also allowed more people to use the application and to order food from our restaurant and others. It helped a lot, because not everyone prefers to pay using a bank card,” he said.
Haat recently expanded into Tel Aviv, taking on Finland’s Wolt, the dominant player in Israel’s food delivery market. Wolt motorbikes zipping along the streets and weaving through dense traffic are an ubiquitous sight in the beachside city.
Now the local competitor is trying to build its own foothold in Tel Aviv using its strengths. “Haat reads the needs of local people because we are local and operate from within,” Kaddan said. “We see what is missing and try to fill those gaps with technology.”

title: Foro Penal reporta el comienzo de excarcelaciones de presos políticos en varios centros de reclusión del país
content:
El vicepresidente de la organización no gubernamental Foro Penal, Gonzalo Himiob Santomé, informó este martes 22 de septiembre de 2026, a las 10:25 pm, que en diferentes centros de reclusión del país se están concretando algunas excarcelaciones de presos políticos.
A través de su cuenta oficial en la red social X (@HimiobSantome), el abogado penalista y activista de derechos humanos puntualizó que el equipo técnico y de abogados de la institución se encuentra en pleno proceso de verificación sobre el terreno para confirmar las identidades y los recintos donde ocurren las liberaciones.

title: From construction site to top of class: Daniel Doe emerges Legon’s best Computer Engineering student
content:
Audio By Carbonatix
Daniel Agudey Doe, a Computer Engineering graduate of the University of Ghana, has emerged as the best graduating student in his programme after navigating significant financial difficulties during his university education.
Before receiving financial assistance through the MTN Ghana Bright Scholarship, Daniel worked on construction sites and took on other manual labour jobs during vacations to raise money for tuition and living expenses.
His financial challenges also affected his ability to meet basic needs on campus, with occasions when he had to skip meals.
“I was simply trying to make it through university. If things became impossible and I had to drop out, at least I could say I had given university my best attempt,” he said.
Daniel entered the University of Ghana with an interest in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning and hoped to eventually build a career in Robotics.
However, the financial demands of university meant that completing his degree was uncertain.
Scholarship eased financial pressure
That changed after he was selected as a beneficiary of the MTN Ghana Bright Scholarship.
The scholarship covered his tuition and hostel fees and provided additional support for his studies.
Daniel said the assistance allowed him to devote more attention to his academic work without having to spend his vacations primarily looking for money to return to school.
“For the first time, I had the privilege many financially stable students have, the ability to focus on my studies without constantly worrying about tuition, hostel fees, or survival,” he said.
With the financial pressure reduced, Daniel said he was able to participate more actively in group studies and devote more time to his coursework.
He eventually graduated as the Best Graduating Computer Engineering Student at the University of Ghana.
Daniel believes the financial support was critical to his completing the programme.
“Without the scholarship, I genuinely do not believe I would have completed university. I may have dropped out as early as Level 200 due to financial pressure,” he said.
From construction to technology
Daniel is currently undertaking his National Service at Amalitech as a Data Engineer.
He intends to build experience in data engineering before moving into Machine Learning and, eventually, Robotics.
He is also considering pursuing a master’s degree in Robotics or a related field combining Robotics and Artificial Intelligence.
Daniel said guidance from his scholarship coordinator, Mr George, also helped him consider his options ahead of his National Service placement.
Scholarship programme
Daniel is among students supported under the MTN Ghana Foundation’s Bright Scholarship programme, which was introduced in 2017.
According to information provided by the foundation, the programme has supported 1,220 students in tertiary institutions across Ghana.
The scholarship covers tuition and accommodation and includes support for a laptop, books and study materials.
The programme has also recorded several academic distinctions among its beneficiaries, with 17 scholars graduating as valedictorians or best students at their institutions and 299 graduating with first-class honours.
For Daniel, his journey from working on construction sites to graduating at the top of his Computer Engineering class demonstrates the difference financial support can make for students facing difficulties in funding their education.
“The MTN Bright Scholarship did not just change my life; it positively impacted my family and my community,” he said.

title: Used Temple Flowers Turn Into Incense Sticks & Biomaterials: Here’s How These Startups Recycle Floral Waste
content: India’s festive season is often marked by color, fragrance, and flowers. From marigold garlands at temples to roses and jasmine used in offerings, flowers are an integral part of many celebrations and rituals. But once the prayers are over and the festivities wind down, large quantities of these flowers are left behind. For a handful of Indian entrepreneurs, that has raised a simple question: can something that has already been part of an important ritual be given a useful second life? Over the years, startups and small enterprises across the country have begun collecting floral waste and turning it into incense, compost, soaps, decorative products and even newer biomaterials. Here are four such ventures looking at flowers not as something to discard, but as a resource that can be reworked. 1. Phool In Kanpur, the idea behind Phool began with a sight that stayed with founder Ankit Agarwal: flowers from temples making their way into the Ganga. Agarwal, along with Prateek Kumar, eventually founded Phool in 2017, building on an idea he had begun exploring a couple of years earlier. In Kanpur, Phool collects temple flowers and transforms them into incense and other products, while also developing flower-based biomaterials. Photograph: (Green Queen Media) The startup collects discarded temple flowers and processes them into products including incense sticks, incense cones and other wellness products. Its research has also led to Fleather, a biomaterial developed from flower waste as an alternative to animal leather. What started as an attempt to address flower waste has therefore grown into a larger circular-economy experiment, combining waste collection, product development and livelihoods. 2. HolyWaste For Maya Vivek and Minal Dalmia, the idea came from seeing that Hyderabad needed a structured way to deal with discarded flowers. The two founded HolyWaste, a venture under Oorvi Sustainable Concepts, in 2018. The women-led enterprise works with temples, flower vendors, event planners and decorators to collect floral waste. The flowers are then sorted, dried and processed through what the company calls its “FloRejuvenation” process. Depending on the material, the flowers can be turned into products such as incense, natural fertilisers, scented cones and soaps. The model also creates work for women involved in sorting and processing the flowers, making the venture as much about livelihoods as waste management. 3. Aaruhi Enterprise In Gurugram, Poonam Sehrawat noticed something while visiting a temple: the flowers offered during prayers were being discarded soon after. She began exploring whether they could be collected and put to another use. HolyWaste collects floral waste from temples, vendors and events, creating products while generating work for women involved in processing. Photograph: (Unesco) In 2019, Sehrawat started Aaruhi Enterprise with Pinki Yadav, focusing on collecting floral waste from temples across Delhi-NCR. The flowers are separated from other waste, processed and handcrafted into products such as dhoop, incense sticks, idols, decorative pieces and air fresheners. Aaruhi also works with women, training them to make floral products and creating opportunities for home-based work. For Sehrawat, what began with a few collection boxes gradually became a small enterprise built around two ideas: reducing floral waste and creating livelihoods. 4. Yuvan In Himachal Pradesh, Ravinder Prashar took a slightly different route. An entrepreneur from Una, Prashar, worked with Dr YS Parmar, University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni, to develop incense sticks using flowers offered at temples. The initiative, launched under the name Yuvan, was supported by Himachal Pradesh’s Chief Minister’s Startup Scheme. The resulting incense uses natural portions and essential oils from flowers, without charcoal or synthetic chemicals. Even the unused floral material can be turned into compost. The prayers may be over, but the flowers can still have a purpose. By reworking what was once discarded, these ventures are giving floral waste a meaningful second life. Photograph: (Indian Wedding Decor Inspiration) The project shows how a familiar material can move through a different cycle: from a flower offered during worship to something that can later become part of another everyday ritual. For these founders, the idea is not to change the traditions around flowers, but to rethink what happens to them afterwards. In doing so, they are showing how something deeply familiar can find a new purpose, long after the prayers and celebrations are over. Sources: '5 Indian Companies Recycling Temple Floral Waste' by Prakati. title: Insula Lacul Morii s-a redeschis. Cum arată noul parc din București și ce facilități au fost amenajate
content:
Foto Insula Lacul Morii s-a redeschis. Cum arată noul parc din București și ce facilități au fost amenajate
Bucureștenii au din nou acces pe Insula Lacul Morii, care a fost redeschisă vineri după finalizarea lucrărilor de modernizare. Zona a fost amenajată ca spațiu pentru plimbare, relaxare, sport și evenimente de mici dimensiuni, iar autoritățile pregătesc și extinderea proiectului cu un parc liniar de aproximativ doi kilometri.
Anunțul a fost făcut de primarul general al Capitalei, Ciprian Ciucu, care a precizat că lucrările au vizat atât insula, cât și digul din apropiere.
„Insula Lacul Morii s-a redeschis astăzi, transformată, bucureștenilor. După ce am refăcut digul, după ce am refăcut Insula, urmează să facem acolo și un mare parc liniar de 2 kilometri. E un sentiment frumos, de împlinire, după ani de pregătire și muncă”, a transmis edilul.
Potrivit autorităților, insula are o suprafață de aproximativ 3,4 hectare, dintre care 2,3 hectare sunt destinate spațiilor verzi. Proiectul include alei, zone de odihnă și locuri în care vizitatorii se pot apropia de apă.
Ciprian Ciucu a anunțat că pe insulă există mai multă umbră, iar vegetația urmează să se dezvolte în următorii ani.
„Aveți acces la apă, mai multă umbră, vegetația va crește, se poate face plajă, se pot face evenimente publice de mici dimensiuni. Sper să vă placă și să o păstrați”, a spus primarul general.
Amenajarea face parte dintr-un proiect mai amplu de regenerare urbană a zonei Lacul Morii, care urmărește transformarea spațiului într-o zonă de agrement și recreere pentru locuitorii Capitalei.
Săptămâna trecută, premierul interimar Ilie Bolojan afirma că investiția are ca obiectiv transformarea terenului neutilizat într-un parc urban modern, cu spații verzi, zone de promenadă și locuri pentru activități sportive.
„Este un proiect care transformă 3,4 hectare de teren neutilizat într-un parc urban modern, cu 2,3 hectare de spațiu verde, în intravilanul Capitalei”, a transmis Bolojan.
El a precizat că investiția este realizată cu fonduri europene, naționale și bani alocați de Sectorul 6, valoarea totală menționată fiind de aproape 59 de milioane de lei.
„Nu e doar despre un lac reamenajat. E despre calitatea vieții oamenilor: un loc de plimbare sigur, un loc pentru sport, o gură de aer proaspăt în mijlocul orașului”, a mai spus premierul interimar.
Modernizarea insulei reprezintă prima etapă a proiectului dedicat zonei Lacul Morii. Autoritățile urmează să continue lucrările pentru amenajarea parcului liniar, care va avea o lungime de aproximativ doi kilometri.

title: AFJA, la organización nacida en Los Ángeles que usa el deporte para abrir oportunidades
content:
AFJA, la organización nacida en Los Ángeles que usa el deporte para abrir oportunidades
AFJA se convirtió en una organización que hoy conecta deporte, educación, cultura y acción social entre Estados Unidos y Centroamérica; conoce más de ella, aquí
La historia de AFJA está estrechamente ligada a Steven Levy Cruz, estadounidense hijo de salvadoreños que durante su infancia pasaba los veranos en el cantón Los Amates, en La Libertad.
Cruz observó desde pequeño las diferencias entre las posibilidades deportivas que encontraba en Los Ángeles y las disponibles para niños de la comunidad salvadoreña. Primero comenzó dejando zapatos y llevando balones en sus viajes.
La iniciativa se transformó posteriormente en un proyecto organizado. AFJA fue creada oficialmente el 5 de julio de 2017, aunque la organización sitúa en 2018 el comienzo de su trabajo continuado mediante academias comunitarias.
Su nombre completo, Academia de Fútbol Juvenil Amatense, conserva la referencia a Los Amates, comunidad donde nació el primer proyecto y donde la familia de Cruz mantenía vínculos desde generaciones anteriores.
La misión inicial fue sencilla: que niños y jóvenes de comunidades con pocos recursos pudieran practicar fútbol de manera organizada sin que el costo del equipo, uniformes o entrenamientos se convirtiera en una barrera.
Con el tiempo, aquella idea dejó de limitarse a entregar implementos. AFJA desarrolló un modelo que vincula la participación deportiva con tres compromisos: rendimiento y asistencia escolar, servicio a la comunidad y presencia constante en entrenamientos y actividades.
De una academia salvadoreña a una red entre Estados Unidos y Centroamérica
Actualmente AFJA se define como una organización juvenil sin fines de lucro con sede en Los Ángeles. Su público principal son niños y jóvenes de comunidades de bajos ingresos tanto del sur de California como de Centroamérica.
La propia organización informa que ha trabajado con más de 800 jóvenes de entre 5 y 23 años. Sus proyectos han tenido presencia en países como El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras y Panamá, además del trabajo comunitario desarrollado en California.
El fútbol sigue siendo la base de AFJA. Una parte fundamental de su sistema consiste en recolectar zapatos, uniformes y otros implementos usados en buenas condiciones en Estados Unidos, limpiarlos y enviarlos a las academias y jóvenes beneficiados.
Las alianzas con clubes estadounidenses han permitido convertir estadios profesionales en puntos de recolección. LA Galaxy, por ejemplo, ha organizado campañas para que sus aficionados entreguen zapatos que posteriormente son redistribuidos entre niños centroamericanos.
El vínculo entre AFJA y el Galaxy ha crecido hasta convertir a la organización en uno de los beneficiarios de la Noche de la Herencia Centroamericana. En distintas ediciones, una parte de cada entrada especial vendida ha sido destinada a sus proyectos.
La edición de septiembre de 2026 alcanzó incluso el agotamiento del paquete especial de entradas destinado a la celebración centroamericana, que incluyó música, danza, elementos culturales y una contribución económica para AFJA.
La organización encontró además una peculiar forma de financiar su trabajo: Pupusas With a Purpose, o Pupusas con propósito. El proyecto vende comida centroamericana en acontecimientos de Los Ángeles y utiliza parte de los ingresos para sostener programas deportivos y educativos.
El puesto evolucionó hasta convertirse en un camión de comida presente regularmente en partidos del LA Galaxy. Sus recetas proceden de miembros de la familia de Cruz e incluyen pupusas, horchata y otros alimentos vinculados con la cultura centroamericana.
AFJA también ha llevado su identidad a otros deportes profesionales. Ha desarrollado Noches de Herencia Salvadoreña con organizaciones vinculadas a Grandes Ligas y la NHL, entre ellas Los Angeles Dodgers y Los Angeles Kings.
Los estadios de MLB han funcionado principalmente como espacios de representación cultural, recaudación y acercamiento de la comunidad a sus programas. El mismo Steven Levy dijo a elsalvador.com "también estamos lanzando un programa de softball y baseball".
En el hockey el trabajo ha avanzado hacia actividades deportivas directas. AFJA ha participado junto con los Kings en clínicas de ball hockey destinadas a niños y familias que no necesitan acceder inicialmente a una costosa pista de hielo.
Los Kings han reconocido públicamente a AFJA como uno de sus aliados para ampliar el acceso al deporte. La Noche de Herencia Salvadoreña del club llegó a vender inicialmente todo su paquete especial de entradas en una de sus ediciones recientes.
La salvadoreña Miley Alfaro participa además como embajadora de hockey de AFJA. Su trabajo ha ampliado los contactos hacia organizaciones como San Jose Sharks, New York Islanders, Anaheim Ducks y Vegas Golden Knights.
Así, aunque el fútbol continúa siendo el eje estructural, AFJA utiliza actualmente el hockey como otra vía de acceso deportivo. El béisbol y otros grandes eventos profesionales funcionan también como escaparates para recaudar fondos y hacer visible a la comunidad.
El impacto supera a la comunidad salvadoreña
Uno de los primeros reconocimientos externos importantes llegó en 2019. Cruz fue elegido MLS WORKS Community MVP, después de una votación entre representantes comunitarios nominados por los clubes de la Major League Soccer.
El reconocimiento entregó 25,000 dólares para AFJA. La MLS destacó entonces la creación de academias en Centroamérica, la reutilización de implementos deportivos y la exigencia de que sus participantes mantuvieran compromiso escolar y comunitario.
Su actuación social tampoco quedó detenida cuando desaparecieron temporalmente los entrenamientos. Durante la pandemia de covid-19, AFJA modificó parte de su operación para apoyar a comunidades salvadoreñas afectadas por la emergencia.
En lugar de medir únicamente goles o partidos disputados, el proyecto intenta utilizar el deporte como incentivo educativo. Los participantes deben mantener asistencia escolar y entregar reportes periódicos, además de colaborar en acciones destinadas a mejorar sus propias comunidades.
AFJA también ha impulsado espacios mixtos para niñas y niños. Desde sus primeros años, la organización planteó el fútbol como herramienta para trabajar valores como responsabilidad, convivencia y equidad entre ambos sexos.
Su impacto en Estados Unidos funciona de otra manera. Además de obtener recursos para Centroamérica, las actividades ofrecen a hijos de inmigrantes un punto de contacto con la cultura de sus familias mediante deporte, comida, música, baile y símbolos nacionales.
La organización ya no trabaja únicamente alrededor de una identidad salvadoreña. Las celebraciones del LA Galaxy pasaron a presentarse como Noches de Herencia Centroamericana, con elementos vinculados también con Guatemala y otros países de la región.
En 2025 y 2026, esas jornadas incluyeron marimba, danzas folclóricas, espacios dedicados a Centroamérica y campañas de recolección de AFJA. El Galaxy mantuvo además la donación de parte de sus paquetes especiales de entradas a la organización.
Otro ejemplo aparece fuera de los estadios. El Los Angeles Times documentó la presencia de Pupusas With a Purpose en Ambiente Central, un espacio creado para reunir a diferentes comunidades centroamericanas de Los Ángeles, no únicamente a salvadoreños.
Eso permite observar una aceptación que supera el núcleo original de AFJA. Clubes, aficionados y organizaciones de otras procedencias han incorporado sus campañas a eventos dirigidos al público centroamericano y latino en general.
No existe, sin embargo, una encuesta independiente que permita afirmar qué piensa en conjunto la comunidad guatemalteca, hondureña, mexicana o estadounidense sobre AFJA. La percepción externa debe medirse, por ahora, mediante señales más concretas.
Entre ellas están las alianzas renovadas durante varios años, paquetes de entradas agotados, campañas de donación dentro de estadios y la permanencia de AFJA en actividades de Galaxy y Kings.
También pesa el reconocimiento de instituciones que no pertenecen a la comunidad salvadoreña. MLS premió a su fundador, Galaxy continúa destinando dinero de sus eventos a la organización y los Kings la presentan como socio para acercar el hockey a nuevas familias.
Casi una década después de su creación, AFJA mantiene así dos espacios de trabajo conectados. En Centroamérica busca que niños con menos recursos tengan deporte organizado; en Estados Unidos utiliza esos mismos deportes para recaudar fondos, fortalecer identidad cultural y acercar nuevas disciplinas a las comunidades latinas.
Su evolución también explica por qué una organización cuyo nombre todavía dice “Fútbol Juvenil Amatense” puede aparecer ahora en un partido de hockey, en un estadio de béisbol o en una fiesta centroamericana de Los Ángeles: el fútbol fue el punto de partida, pero el objetivo terminó siendo más amplio que una cancha.
La asociación AFJA acerca mediante el deporte y la convivencia sana a los chicos de pocas posibilidades para que puedan practicar uno e integrarse a una comunidad que crece todos los días en los Estados Unidos, gracias a la iniciativa de un salvadoreño visionario, sencillo y comprometido: Steven Levy
